package_info.package_versions: Outdated Magento CMS versions on 80 e-commerce sites
package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript code on compromised Magento e-commerce sites captures customers’ payment information during checkout and exfiltrates it to attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling credit card theft and fraudulent transactions.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, specifically when the checkout page loads and the customer submits the payment form
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript in Magento checkout templates (e.g., app/design/frontend/base/default/template/checkout/onepage.phtml) or via unauthorized third-party JS includes

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the checkout form is submitted, the code hooks into the form submission event, programmatically reads credit card fields from the DOM, and sends the captured payment data via HTTP POST to a hardcoded malicious domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts sensitive payment data directly from the checkout form and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled server, which is a hallmark of web skimming and data exfiltration attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted, authorized payment processors or gateways, never to unknown or untrusted third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate e-commerce sites may send form data to payment gateways or fraud detection services, but only to vetted, trusted endpoints and never to domains not associated with the business or payment provider.
key_indicators: Direct DOM access to credit card input fields during form submission
Network requests (HTTP POST) to hardcoded, untrusted external domains
JavaScript injected into checkout templates or loaded from unauthorized third-party sources
Absence of user notification or consent for data transmission to external domains

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits vulnerabilities in outdated Magento CMS to gain unauthorized write access to e-commerce site files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to inject malicious JavaScript into checkout page templates or include unauthorized third-party scripts

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into checkout page templates (such as app/design/frontend/base/default/template/checkout/onepage.phtml) or loaded as a third-party script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimming code in customers’ browsers during checkout

attack_chain.action: When a customer loads the checkout page and submits payment, the malicious script captures credit card data and exfiltrates it to the attacker’s server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment data for use in fraud or resale on underground markets

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code accessing payment form fields (e.g., credit card number, expiry, CVV) and sending data to external, non-payment domains
Unexpected network requests (HTTP POST) from checkout pages to domains not associated with legitimate payment processors
Modification of checkout templates or inclusion of unknown third-party scripts in checkout page source code
file_indicators: Presence of unknown or suspicious JavaScript files in the webroot or loaded by checkout pages
References to external scripts or domains in the checkout page source that are not part of the official payment workflow
network_indicators: POST requests from checkout pages to domains not associated with payment processors (e.g., https://malicious-domain.com/collect)
Unusual outbound traffic to newly registered or untrusted domains during checkout form submission
Network requests containing payment data fields (cc, exp, cvv) in the payload
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to checkout template files and unexpected third-party JavaScript includes. Use file integrity monitoring on Magento template files to detect changes. Analyze network traffic from checkout pages for POST requests to unknown or untrusted domains, especially those containing payment data fields. Employ web application firewalls to block or alert on suspicious outbound requests from e-commerce pages. Regularly audit the source code of checkout pages for unauthorized script inclusions or references to external domains.
